title: bug: the deploy receipt's refusal detail reaches a screen unredacted, so a health-check failure can print a connection string
description:
Filed by worker-4d8571e7 from task-85895a88a2484d8589046b2030efd445 (the Needs-you incident card) as an out-of-scope finding. NOT fixable in that row: the redaction seam is daemon-side and that row is confined to the control room, and the incident card is REQUIRED by its DoD 1 to render the line VERBATIM - a browser-side scrub would be the wrong layer and would break the property it was built to guarantee.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04, 2026-09-08):
- apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts:247 `errorLineOf` serves `line: receipt.refusal.detail` straight off the last refusing deploy receipt.
- `grep -rn "redact\|REDACT" apps/daemon/src/deployment/*.ts apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts` returned NOTHING. Same for apps/daemon/src/secrets/.
- The control-room decoder (live-deployments-health.ts `errorLineOf`) carries the line through unchanged BY DESIGN, and two surfaces now render it: environments-section.tsx (`cr.environments.card.<env>.error`) and the new incident card (`cr.needsyou.incident.<env>#<id>.error`).

So there is NO redaction anywhere between the receipt write and the DOM. Epic rail 3 says a secret never surfaces in plaintext - not on a screen, not in an error path. A deploy or health-check refusal detail is exactly the kind of string that carries `postgres://user:password@host`, a registry token in a docker pull error, or a bearer header echoed by an upstream 401.

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN and must be measured before planning: whether any refusal detail the deploy engine actually mints can contain an interpolated secret. That measurement is the first step, not an assumption - if no path can, the right outcome is a committed arm pinning that, not a scrubber.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS: at the receipt-writing seam in the daemon, which is the only layer that knows what a secret is (it holds the environment variable values). Scrubbing at the read, or in the browser, would leave the plaintext durable in the event store.

Not in scope for this row: the incident card, the Environments section, or the health read's shape.
definitionOfDone: Measure first: enumerate every string that can become a deploy receipt's `refusal.detail` and state, path by path, which ones can carry an interpolated environment value, a URL with credentials, or an auth header. Record the commands and their output. If NONE can, the deliverable is a committed arm that pins that property, not a scrubber.

If any path can, redaction happens where the secret is known - at the receipt write in the daemon - so the plaintext is never durable in the event store. A scrub at the read or in the browser is not acceptable: it leaves the secret on disk.

A committed test asserts a receipt whose refusal detail contains a credential-bearing URL is stored redacted, asserting the exact redaction marker and that the secret substring is absent - not merely that the string changed.

The incident card and the Environments section keep rendering the line VERBATIM as served. Neither surface gains a scrubber; assert both still show the daemon's line unchanged (task-85895a88a2484d8589046b2030efd445 owns those arms).

DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH QA'S ATTENTION:
- Value-free assertions throughout: `expectRedacted` compares BOOLEANS (`actual === REDACTED`), never `expect(actual).toBe(...)`, because a `toBe` failure prints the raw actual string into a log. Same for `expectAbsentFromBytes` (Buffer.includes -> boolean).
- `REDACTED` is restated as a literal in the test, deliberately NOT imported: an arm importing the production constant would follow it to any other value and stay green.
